summary: Iteration 14 — RETEST after fix. 16/16 tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration13_push_broadcast.py. The audience-filter bug in routes/broadcast.py (now using `approval_status` with legacy `status` fallback via $or) is resolved: POST /api/admin/broadcasts {audience:'all'} returns 201 with recipient_count >= 2 against two freshly-approved TEST_ users; segmented audiences (providers/vendors empty → 400 as documented; users → 201). The announcement thread is fan-out for each recipient and surfaces under GET /api/chat/threads with is_announcement=true. Non-super-admin POST to the announcement thread returns 403 with detail mentioning 'announcement'/'one-way'. GET /api/chat/{tid}/details exposes is_announcement=true. Duplicate Operation ID `search_messages` warning is no longer emitted after backend restart (only present in pre-fix log lines 4714/4770; latest startup at 12:18 is clean). Push relay 401s with placeholder EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY remain non-blocking as designed.
critical_code_review_comments: broadcast.py:_audience_user_ids now uses an $or over [approval_status, status] to cover both schemas — sane and minimally invasive. Recommend a follow-up data-migration sweep to backfill `approval_status` from any legacy `status` rows so the $or fallback becomes redundant.
chat.py — duplicate `search_messages` definition removed; only the original at line 532 remains. OpenAPI schema is clean on restart.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration13_push_broadcast.py (test-only fix: announcement-thread assertion now scans the thread's full message list for the original broadcast text instead of relying on last_message, because a later segmented audience='users' broadcast legitimately overwrites last_message)
seed_data_creation: Two fresh TEST_alice_* and TEST_bob_* users are registered and approved on every run (per-test-module fixture). They persist in the DB after the run; admin may purge them via the existing demo-user purge mechanism.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Broadcast/announcement flow is fully green. Test file is idempotent. EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY 401s in backend logs are expected with the placeholder key and are swallowed by routes/push.py without breaking primary flows.
rca_of_issue: Original RCA (iteration 13): audience filter queried `status` while users wrote `approval_status` → broadcasts always 400. Fix in iteration 14 (by main agent): broadcast.py now matches users via $or over both keys, so newly-approved users (approval_status) AND any legacy rows (status) both receive broadcasts. Test-side adjustment in iteration 14: the announcement-thread assertion was made robust to the second segmented broadcast that also targets plain users, by scanning the message list rather than only last_message.
